name: Croatia
synopsis: Plenković's third government relies on the nationalist Homeland Movement, with frequent clashes with President Milanović over foreign policy.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
system: Federal parliamentary republic with tripartite presidency (Dayton system, international High Representative)

headOfState.name: Tripartite Presidency: Denis Bećirović (Bosniak, SDP), Darijana Filipović (Croat, HDZ BiH), Željka Cvijanović (Serb, SNSD)
headOfState.title: Presidency (preliminary Oct 2026 results)

headOfGovernment.name: Borjana Krišto
headOfGovernment.title: Chair of the Council of Ministers

judiciary: Constitutional Court (with international judges); High Representative Christian Schmidt holds 'Bonn powers'.

elections.name: General election
elections.note: Provisional until certified by the Central Election Commission.

synopsis: Nationalist parties largely held their ground in the October 2026 general election. Government formation at state and entity level follows, with Republika Srpska secessionist rhetoric a persistent risk.
policies: EU accession reforms (talks opened conditionally in 2024)
reviewNote: Confirm certified presidency results and new Council of Ministers.

name: Serbia
system: Unitary parliamentary republic (strong presidency in practice)

headOfState.name: Ana Brnabić
headOfState.title: Acting President (Speaker of the National Assembly; Vučić resigned Sept 2026)

governingParties: Student List expected to form the next government

legislature.name: National Assembly (250)
legislature.control: Student List majority (140 of 250) in the newly elected assembly
legislature.detail: Final results adopted by the electoral commission (RIK) on 5 November 2026: Student List 140, Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia 103, national-minority lists 7. The new assembly must hold its constitutive session by 5 December 2026; until then Ana Brnabić (SNS) remains Speaker.

judiciary: Constitutional Court; judiciary under political pressure.

elections.name: Snap parliamentary election
elections.note: Student-led opposition list defeated Vučić's SNS, winning 140 of 250 seats; turnout about 69%. Vučić conceded.

elections.name: Early presidential election (due after Vučić's resignation; must be held by 27 December 2026, not yet called)

synopsis: In a seismic shift, the student-led opposition movement that grew out of protests over the 2024 Novi Sad canopy collapse defeated Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party on 25 October 2026, ending more than a decade of SNS dominance. Vučić, who resigned the presidency in September to run for prime minister, conceded on election night. Final results on 5 November gave the Student List 140 of 250 seats; Speaker Ana Brnabić is acting President and Đuro Macut leads a caretaker government until the new assembly elects a government.
policies: EU accession while managing ties with Russia and China
challenges: Forming a government from a list of political newcomers
A peaceful transfer of power and SNS-aligned institutions
Acting presidency and early presidential election
Kosovo dispute and NIS oil company sanctions
reviewNote: Map leader set to the acting President: while the government is a caretaker one, Brnabić holds the transition's main levers (convening the new assembly, proposing the prime minister after consultations, calling the presidential election). Unconfirmed: whether the acting presidency passes to the new Speaker once the new assembly elects one, and who the Student List will propose as prime minister.

name: Montenegro
judiciary: Constitutional Court; judicial appointments were long blocked.
synopsis: Montenegro is the front-runner for EU accession, aiming to close negotiations by 2026–27.

name: Kosovo

legislature.name: Assembly (120)
legislature.detail: Elected Justina Shiroka Pula president on 7 October 2026 with 81 votes (80 needed), averting dissolution.

elections.name: Presidential election (by the Assembly)
elections.note: Justina Shiroka Pula, proposed by Kurti and backed by Vetëvendosje and PDK, elected in the first round with 81 votes in a vote around the midnight constitutional deadline.

synopsis: Kurti formed a new government in September 2026 after a long deadlock, and on 7 October the Assembly elected Justina Shiroka Pula president at the constitutional deadline, averting another snap election. The vote followed an agreement between Vetëvendosje and the PDK, under which the Assembly first passed amendments limiting the powers of the Hague-based Kosovo Specialist Chambers.
policies: EU visa liberalisation and membership bid
challenges: Specialist Chambers law amendments (possible constitutional review)

name: Albania
synopsis: Rama aims to complete EU accession talks by 2027 and has appointed an AI 'minister' for procurement oversight.

name: North Macedonia
synopsis: The nationalist government resists Bulgaria's demand for a constitutional change recognising a Bulgarian minority, stalling EU talks.

name: Turkey
judiciary: Constitutional Court and Court of Cassation; judiciary widely seen as politicised.
synopsis: Erdoğan's government faces a resurgent CHP opposition whose leading figure, Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, has been jailed since March 2025. A peace process with the PKK is under way.

name: Georgia

legislature.name: Parliament (150)
legislature.detail: Main opposition boycotting; several opposition parties face ban proceedings.

judiciary: Constitutional Court; judiciary considered captured by ruling party.
synopsis: Georgian Dream, founded by billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili, has frozen EU accession and cracked down on protest and civil society.

name: Armenia

legislature.name: National Assembly (105)
legislature.detail: June 2026: Civil Contract ~49.8%; Strong Armenia (Karapetyan) and Armenia Alliance (Kocharyan) in opposition.

synopsis: Pashinyan won a renewed majority in June 2026, framing it as a mandate for peace with Azerbaijan and distancing Armenia from Moscow.
policies: Peace treaty with Azerbaijan (Aug 2025 Washington framework, TRIPP corridor)
New constitution (required by Baku for treaty signing)
challenges: Tensions with the Armenian Apostolic Church

name: Azerbaijan
judiciary: Constitutional Court; courts controlled by executive.
synopsis: Aliyev, having retaken Karabakh in 2023, is negotiating a peace treaty with Armenia while strengthening ties with the US and Turkey and clashing with Russia.
policies: Peace treaty and transit corridor with Armenia
